newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FOCUS-Manila bourse gains ground but new cloud looms.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Manila bourse gains ground but new cloud looms.

text.p: The Philippine stock market ended one of its worst weeks with a mini-rally on Friday but a foreign broker's advise to investors to dump shares cast fresh gloom on the still wobbly market, analysts said.

Spurred by banks and commercial-industrial issues, the main index finished 27.76 points, or 0.94 percent up, at 2,976.78 points in a second straight day of what brokers said was a technically induced rally.
The main index suffered a weekly loss of 2.7 percent from 3,060.59 last Friday.
Since March 31, when the downturn began the index has lost 7.6 percent. The index was at 3,222.98 on March 31.
The property sector, hammered by rumours that sent the market reeling, again suffered a slump after Thursday's rebound and shed 7.74 points to end at 1,417.93 points.
The still fragile market, which analysts said would likely remain defensive next week, suffered a fresh blow when brokerage Asia Equity sent out a "Sell the Philippines" advisory to clients.
"Heady earnings expectations of 30 percent can only disappoint. And interest rates are too low ... Our sell view on the market is predicated on valuation and earnings expectations," it said.
The recommendations made by Asia Equity's chief strategist Ian MacFarlene, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters, said the market was already fully valued and interest rates were too low.
Some analysts quickly slammed the report, saying its release to the public could only dampen a market yearning for even the smallest bit of cheerful news.

"At this time what we need is all the encouragement ... that's a very unwarranted type of report," said Irving Ackerman, president of Ackerman Inc. He said he was not criticising the brokerage for preparing such a report to its clients but regretted it had reached media hands.
"Some of them (investors) will not pay attention to it but some will probably really get scared and wonder what to do," he said.
Villamor Vital, chief economist for All-Asia Capital and Trust Corp, said the report was scary, adding, "Right now, it's already scaring me."
"I think this report will have an impact on foreign and institutional investors in terms of really following their recommendation," Vital said.
Liza Joson, research head at Amsteel Securities Phils Inc, said the market's performance on Friday showed it was still susceptible to selling due to weak sentiment on the property sector.
The sector had been hit by speculation of a crash in real estate prices due to a reported condominium glut, igniting fears the Philippines might be treading Thailand's path.
A property oversupply in Thailand had badly hit Thai banks because of their huge loans to real estate firms in that country.
Vital said he disagreed with views that the property sector was facing trouble.
"I do not share the view that others have been spreading that there is a cloud over the property sector," Vital told Reuters. "I've always thought the sector still has some upside potential."
Vital said he believed the downtrend in the property sector in the past several months had been "largely technical."
